premises: Surface oxidation and defects on melt-spun ribbons act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for primary crystallization.
An ultrathin SiO2 coating can passivate the surface and suppress heterogeneous nucleation.
Suppressing surface nucleation increases amorphous fraction and thermal stability during reheating.
Physical vapor deposition can produce a uniform, adherent ~50 nm SiO2 coating on the alloy immediately after quenching.
The crystallization onset temperature in DSC will shift upward if surface nucleation is suppressed.
